full_judgment:
Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, j:- 'This Appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 and 20.02.2006 respectively delivered by the learned Joint District Judge 3rd Court, Tangail in Other Class Suit No.10 of 2002 which has been dismissed on contest. 

 7. The learned Advocate for the appellant also submits that the learned Trial Court below erred in law and in facts in decreeing the suit upon misreading and non reading the evidence on record and moreover if upon proper consideration of facts, circumstances and evidences on record the learned Joint District Judge ought to have dismissed the suit because of the fact that the letter dated 21.4.2002 was never acted upon. 

 12. The learned Advocate for the appellant again submits that the Plaintiff was asked to deposit defoliated money to School fund as per resolution adopted by Managing Committee the competent authority of the school which was taken in pursuance of Boards Suggestion to reconcile the matter with the plaintiff but that was not complied with by the plaintiff. The learned Advocate for the appellant then submits that the learned Court below misread the deposition of DW. 2, the DW-2 admitted in cross examination that "Abul Quashem is Headmaster in Charge "আবুল কাশেম ভারপ্রাপ্ত প্রধান শিক্ষক” The witness furthermore replied in cross that he did not accompany the plaintiff when he joined and did not see which works was done by him on that day. The learned Advocate for the appellant again submits that having regard to the fact that Managing Committee on 14.6.1999 the respondent No. 1 against suspension filed a writ petition and obtained Rule and stay order but alter hearing the Rule has been discharged, thereafter the managing Committee dismissed the Plaintiff respondent No.1 on various allegation of misconduct/ misappropriation of school fund and sought approval of the Education Board and during pendency of the same he filed a suit which was rejected as premature and not maintainable and on an appeal the High Court Division interfered with the order and directed to hear the suit on merit and as such the suit proceeded but the issue of maintainability was not resolved by the Trial Court and respondent No. 1 got the decree and in that view of the matter the trial Court committed error of law in decreeing the suit. The learned Advocate for the appellant further submits that the trial Court committed error of law in decreeing the suit giving emphasis of the order of injunction regard to the fact that the order of injunction was stayed by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court in C.P. No.1753 of 2002 and the Appellate Division granted leave by order dated 29.1.2003 and the appellant riled C.A. I89 of 2003 and the Appellate Division extended the stay order till disposal of the said Appeal which is still pending and in such view of the matter the trial Court misconceived in coming to the finding and decision that the plaintiff/respondent is functioning at the strength of injunction granted by the High Court. The learned Advocate for the appellant lastly submits that the learned trial Court gave emphasis on the order of the High Court but failed to consider that the Hon'ble Appellate Division granted leave on the ground that the High Court Division erred in law in not following the judicial principles in respect of granting temporary injunction illegally acted on some fake and forged papers in making the Rule absolute and that resolution dated 24.12.2000 of dismissal adopted by the managing committee was sent to the Board for approval but the Appeal and Arbitration Committee of the Board keeping the matter in abeyance for long time directed to compromise which is without jurisdiction and the respondent No. 1 upon misleading the Court obtained the order of injunction in as much as from the date of his suspension on 14.6.99 an acting headmaster is functioning as headmaster in charge of the said school and the respondent No.1 is not entitled to have an order of injunction in as much as he has no prima-facie arguable case nor he is holding the office of the headmaster since 14.6.99 nor the balance of convenience and inconvenience is in his favour. 

 14. Heard the learned Advocates for both the sides, perused the impugned judgment and decree and other connected documents. It also perused the letter of the Arbitration Committee where it is directed that the respondent as well as the defendant-appellant come to mutual independent decision over the matter. In the following reference 

 15. Perused the Memo No. 3933 (4) addressed to the Headmaster in charge by inspector of school, Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Dhaka. On perusal of said Memo it is very much clear that the Arbitration Committee has been empowered to look into any dispute arise the extract of the letter has already been quoted herein to clarify the provision of law in this regard. The learned Joint District Judge while passing the impugned judgment and order in Other Class Suit No. 10 of 2002 totally over looked the aforesaid Memo issued from the Board of Secondary and higher Secondary Education Dhaka and without taking into account and consider the aforesaid Memo by the Joint District Judge passed the impugned judgment in violation of the rules and regulation as contained in the concerned rule of the Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Dhaka. In that view of the matter the judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge in Other Class Suit No.10 of 2010 is not sustainable in law and as such we find substance and merit in the submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant. On the other hand the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent could not establish his case. In that view of the matter we find merit in the submission as advanced by the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant- and find no merit in the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent. 

 16. In the result the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 decree signed on 20.02.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court Tangail is hereby set aside and the original Title Suit No. 10 of 2002 is hereby dismissed with cost.
